look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Look for low, fan-shaped, pleated leaves arising near the ground with smooth unarmed petioles, then check the branching flower or fruit stalks rising through and often above the crown.
taxonomy_notes: Accepted Sabal minor (Jacq.) Pers. in POWO; do not confuse with trunk-forming Sabal mexicana or ornamental Washingtonia palms.

project_inclusion.notes: County-level native-range certification deferred; no native-only metric inclusion.

morphology_keys.habit: Low fan palm with mostly subterranean trunk, commonly forming a short ground-level crown.
morphology_keys.leaves_attachment: Costapalmate fan leaves with many deeply divided, narrow segments; petioles lack marginal spines.
morphology_keys.flower_reproductive: Large branching panicles bearing numerous small pale flowers, sometimes extending beyond leaves.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: Small round dark fruits on branching stalks; close-up needed for confident fruit-stage comparisons.
morphology_keys.stem_bud: Usually lacks a tall exposed trunk; leaf bases clustered low.

confused_with: Sabal mexicana (usually tall exposed trunk at maturity)
Washingtonia robusta (spiny petiole margins and often a tall trunk)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Subterranean/short trunk and unarmed fan-leaf petioles, corroborated by inflorescence.
